increment_operators.quote: It counts from 1 to 5; so it prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; For i from 1 to n means do it for each number
increment_operators.rule: wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. Right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written.

loop_body.quote: It counts from 1 to 5; so it prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; For i from 1 to n means do it for each number
loop_body.rule: wrong rule: The computer fills in omitted steps or values that the programmer meant, e.g. REPEAT 4 [FORWARD 30] draws a square without a turn command. Right rule: The computer executes only what the code states; every needed step and value must be written.

loop_variable.quote: It counts from 1 to 5; For i from 1 to n means do it for each number
loop_variable.rule: wrong rule: Changing the loop variable inside the body does not affect the loop condition; the loop still runs its planned number of times. Right rule: The condition is tested with the current value of the variable, including changes made in the body.

evidence.logic: Folk meaning: English 'for each ...' or 'for 10 times' names a whole collection or a count to be handled at once, and a maths reading treats the header as simultaneous conditions. A Java for is a while loop in compact form: one init, then test-body-update repeated, one pass at a time.
